 10735	  \label{thm:degAt_relPicToPicEt}
 10736	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.degAt_relPicToPicEt}
 10737	  \uses{def:degAt, thm:picEtMap_relPicToPicEt, thm:picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt,
 10738	    thm:degAff_unit, def:relPicToPicEt, def:relPicMap}
 10739	  \leanok
 10740	  For a test object \(T\), a relative Picard class \(z \in \mathrm{relPic}(C,T)\) and a
 10741	  field point \(t \colon \Spec K \to T\), the degree at \(t\) of the unit image of \(z\) is
 10742	  the relative degree of the restriction:
 10743	  \[
 10744	    \deg_t\bigl(\mathrm{relPicToPicEt}(z)\bigr) = \mathrm{relPicDeg}_K\bigl(t^{*} z\bigr).
 10745	  \]
 10746	\end{theorem}

 10748	  \leanok
 10749	  Naturality of the unit (Theorem~\ref{thm:picEtMap_relPicToPicEt}) collapses the
 10750	  restriction along \(t\) to the unit image of \(t^{*}z\) over \(\Spec K\); affine
 10751	  consistency (Theorem~\ref{thm:picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt}) identifies its affine
 10752	  collapse with the plus unit of \(t^{*}z\); the unit normalization of the degree
 10753	  (Theorem~\ref{thm:degAff_unit}) reads \(\mathrm{relPicDeg}_K\).
 10754	\end{proof}

 10756	\begin{definition}[The Abel \v Cech class]
 10757	  \label{def:abelCechClass}

 10759	  \uses{def:graphLocalEquations, def:relPicToPicEt, def:relPic}
 10760	  \leanok
 10761	  \source{kleiman-picard, abelian-varieties:page-0107}
 10762	  Let \(P \colon \mathbf{1} \to C\) be a rational point of the curve (a morphism from the
 10763	  unit test). The \emph{Abel \v Cech class} on the test \(T = C\) is
 10764	  \[
 10765	    \mathcal A_P \;:=\; \struct{C \otimes C}(\Delta) \cdot \struct{C \otimes C}(P \times C)^{-1}
 10766	      \;\in\; \Pic(C \otimes C),
 10767	  \]
 10768	  the graph class of the identity \(\id_C\) (the diagonal) times the inverse graph class of
 10769	  the constant point \(C \to \mathbf 1 \xrightarrow{P} C\) — both factors through the graph
 10770	  divisor of Definition~\ref{def:graphLocalEquations}, so one degree certificate serves
 10771	  both. The \emph{Abel class} \(\alpha_P \in \mathrm{picEt}(C, C)\) is the unit image of its
 10772	  relative class. Milne's cited section assumes \(g(C)>0\); this graph-class construction
 10773	  uses only the rational point \(P\) and therefore also applies in genus zero.
 10774	\end{definition}

 10776	\begin{theorem}[The functor-point formula, \v Cech level]
 10777	  \label{thm:cechPicMap_abelCechClass}
 10778	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.cechPicMap_abelCechClass}
 10779	  \uses{def:abelCechClass, thm:graphLocalEquations_base_change}
 10780	  \leanok
 10781	  For any test \(T\) and any point \(f \colon T \to C\), the pullback of the Abel \v Cech
 10782	  class along \(C \lhd f\) is the graph-minus-constant-graph class of \(f\):
 10783	  \[
 10784	    (C \lhd f)^{*} \mathcal A_P
 10785	      = \struct{C \otimes T}(\Gamma_f)\cdot\struct{C \otimes T}(\Gamma_{P_T})^{-1},
 10786	  \]
 10787	  where \(P_T \colon T \to \mathbf 1 \xrightarrow{P} C\) is the constant point of \(T\).
 10788	\end{theorem}
 10789	\begin{proof}
 10790	  \leanok
 10791	  Base change of the graph class (Theorem~\ref{thm:graphLocalEquations_base_change}) sends
 10792	  \(\struct{}(\Gamma_{\id_C})\) to \(\struct{}(\Gamma_{f \circ \id}) = \struct{}(\Gamma_f)\)
 10793	  and \(\struct{}(\Gamma_{P_C})\) to \(\struct{}(\Gamma_{f \circ P_C})\); and
 10794	  \(f \circ P_C = P_T\) by terminality of the unit test (both factor through
 10795	  \(\mathbf 1\)). Pullback is a homomorphism, so the product formula follows.
 10796	\end{proof}

 10799	  \label{thm:degAt_abelPicEt}

 10803	  \leanok

 10805	  \(\deg_t(\alpha_P) = 0\). The certificate is a proved equality at every point — no
 10806	  choice is involved.
 10807	\end{theorem}

 10809	  \leanok

 10811	  \(\mathrm{relPicDeg}_K\) of the restriction of the relative Abel class along \(t\), which
 10812	  the relative degree reads as \(\deg_{\Pic}\) of the fibre \v Cech class
 10813	  (Definition~\ref{def:relPicDeg} on the projected representative,
 10814	  Definition~\ref{def:relPicMap}). By the functor-point formula
 10815	  (Theorem~\ref{thm:cechPicMap_abelCechClass}) at \(f := t\), the fibre class is
 10816	  \(\struct{}(\Gamma_t) \cdot \struct{}(\Gamma_{P_{\Spec K}})^{-1}\) — the ratio of two
 10817	  graph classes of \(K\)-points. Each has degree one by the degree-one certificate
 10818	  (Theorem~\ref{thm:classDeg_graphPicClass}), so the degree is \(1 - 1 = 0\).
 10819	\end{proof}

 10823	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.abelElement, AlgebraicGeometry.abelElement_coe}
 10824	  \uses{def:pic0Subgroup, thm:degAt_abelPicEt, def:abelCechClass}
 10825	  \leanok
 10826	  \source{kleiman-picard, abelian-varieties:page-0107}
 10827	  The \emph{Abel element} is the Abel class as an element of the degree-zero subgroup,
 10828	  \[
 10829	    \alpha_P \in \mathrm{pic}^0(C, C),
 10830	  \]
 10831	  membership being the certificate of Theorem~\ref{thm:degAt_abelPicEt}. On points it is the
 10832	  family \(t \mapsto [\,\Gamma_t - \Gamma_P\,]\), the divisor-class form \(t \mapsto [t - P]\)
 10833	  of the Abel map with base point \(P\). As above, Milne states this formula under the
 10834	  standing hypothesis \(g(C)>0\), whereas the formal element is defined in genus zero as
 10835	  well.
 10836	\end{definition}

 10841	  \uses{def:abelElement, thm:picEtMap_relPicToPicEt, thm:cechPicMap_abelCechClass,
